messages:
Jamie: Heads up—CI went red on linux after I merged the ccache tweak a few minutes ago. Failing targets are mostly CMake-based native libs in //third_party:build. Can't repro locally yet.
DevBot: [CI] build (linux-x86-64) failed — https://ci.internal.redwood/rls/3421 (log attached)
Jamie: paste log snippet:
```
[ 87%] Linking CXX shared library libnative.so
/usr/bin/ld: /workspace/_bazel/jenkins/.../libstuff.a(stuff.o): undefined reference to `pthread_mutex_lock'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```
Jamie: looks like a missing -lpthread during link. This started right after the ccache config change in tools/toolchain/ccache.bzl — cc_cache is now wrapping the compiler with a wrapper sh script.
Liam: can you re-run with CCACHE_DISABLE=1 to confirm? if it goes green that points to the wrapper dropping -pthread or changing linking order.
Jamie: re-run kicked off: https://ci.internal.redwood/rls/3424 — disabling ccache for the job now.
DevBot: [CI] build (linux-x86-64) re-run queued
Sara: I hit a very similar link error earlier when a wrapper script reset LDFLAGS. Quick check: does the wrapper exec the compiler with `"$@"` or does it recompose args? If it reconstructs arguments it can drop `-pthread` which is often passed by CMake as a separate flag.
Jamie: good call — the wrapper uses `exec ${CCACHE_BIN} \"$@\"` in the bump, but I modified it to normalize PATH first. Not confident on quoting there.
Kyle: I'll take a bisect if needed. Steps I'll run:
```
git fetch origin
git bisect start HEAD $(git rev-parse origin/main~5)
# mark bad at HEAD, then mark good at a known good commit
# build with ccache enabled to reproduce
CCACHE_DISABLE=0 bazel build //third_party/... --config=linux
```
Liam: if bisect shows the ccache commit, we should revert the wrapper change and publish a patch to ensure we preserve exact argv forwarding. Also test with `-Wl,--no-as-needed`? maybe not necessary.
Jamie: FYI local quick test: I copied the wrapper and replaced `exec ${CCACHE_BIN} "${"$@"}"` with `exec ${CCACHE_BIN} "${"$@"}"` (same) 🤦; need to test with `set -x` to see final args. Will push more logs.
Sara: can you also try `bazel build //third_party:build -- sandbox_debug --experimental_strict_action_env` to see env differences? sometimes ccache wrapper changes TMP or HOME.
Jamie: started another CI run with `export CCACHE_DISABLE=1` and `--sandbox_debug`. Link: https://ci.internal.redwood/rls/3426
DevBot: [CI] build (linux-x86-64) re-run failed — same undefined reference in log 3426
Liam: OK, not just ccache disabling. Could be the wrapper altering LD flags or our toolchain rule change earlier today. Any recent changes to cmake toolchain or our bazel cc_toolchain? 
Jamie: There was a small tweak in //tools:cc_toolchain_defs yesterday to normalize `linker_flag` ordering.
Kyle: I'll run a local build matrix across the last 10 commits and report back by EOD. If someone can bisect to narrow to 1 commit that's faster—I'll help run the builds.
Sara: If we need a hotfix, we can revert the toolchain change first (safer) and then bisect ccache later.
Jamie: Agree. Created PR to revert toolchain tweak: https://git.internal.redwood/r/redwood/cc-toolchain/pull/218 (draft). Can someone review quickly? @Liam @Kyle
Liam: on it, will review in 15.
Kyle: ping me if CI still red after revert, I'll prioritize bisecting.
Jamie: thanks all. I'll attach the full CI log and my local strace output in the PR. (reacted with :eyes: by Liam)
_meta: generated slack thread about CI link errors after ccache/toolchain changes
